package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally crafted to exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the CDNJS automated update infrastructure, enabling arbitrary file write and remote code execution on Cloudflare's CDNJS servers. This could lead to full compromise of the CDNJS infrastructure, affecting millions of websites.

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate (CI/CD bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) with malicious file paths

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (bash script, delivered via crafted archive path)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Places a shell script outside the intended extraction directory using path traversal, enabling arbitrary code execution on the server when the script is executed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of path traversal sequences (../../../../) in archive file paths is a classic indicator of an attempt to escape the intended extraction directory, which is a well-known attack vector ('ZIP Slip').
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should only contain files within their own directory structure. This package attempts to write files to arbitrary locations on the server.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Path traversal in archive files is almost never legitimate in package distribution.
key_indicators: Files written to /tmp or other system directories
Presence of executable scripts outside package scope

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate (CI/CD bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) with malicious symlink

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: symlink in git repo pointing to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd or config files)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Creates a symbolic link in the repository that, when processed by the bot, allows reading of arbitrary files from the server filesystem.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Symlinks in package repositories that point outside the package directory are a known method for arbitrary file read attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not contain symlinks to sensitive system files or files outside their own directory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Symlinks are sometimes used for internal package structure, but never to system files.
key_indicators: Symlinks pointing to /etc, /tmp, or other sensitive locations
Symlinks present in package root or unexpected locations

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate (CI/CD bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) with path traversal to overwrite scripts

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (bash script, delivered via crafted archive path)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Overwrites a script that is regularly executed by the CDNJS update bot, enabling persistent arbitrary command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overwriting system or automation scripts via path traversal is a direct method to gain persistent code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Package updates should never overwrite automation or system scripts outside their own directory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for this behavior in package management.
key_indicators: Archive entries targeting automation or system scripts
Unexpected changes to bot or CI/CD scripts after package update

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a new npm package (hey-sven) with maliciously crafted archive paths (path traversal and symlinks).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious files and symlinks are included in the package archive.

attack_chain.action: CDNJS autoupdate bot downloads and extracts the new package version, processing the malicious archive.
attack_chain.leads_to: Path traversal and symlink payloads are written to arbitrary locations on the server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious scripts are executed by the bot or automation system, or sensitive files are read via symlink.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution and/or access to sensitive secrets (API keys, tokens).

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen secrets (GITHUB_REPO_API_KEY, WORKERS_KV_API_TOKEN) to tamper with CDNJS libraries, cache, or website.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of CDNJS infrastructure and potential supply-chain attack on all users.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction with file paths containing multiple '../' sequences
Symlinks in package archives pointing outside the package directory
Unexpected file writes or overwrites in /tmp or automation script directories
Execution of scripts extracted from package archives outside intended scope
file_indicators: npm package tarballs (.tgz) with path traversal entries
Symlinks in package repositories pointing to sensitive files
Overwritten automation or CI/CD scripts after package update
network_indicators: Unusual access to internal API endpoints using newly extracted secrets
Unexpected outbound connections from automation bots after package update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package archives containing path traversal sequences in file paths (e.g., '../../../'). Block or alert on symlinks in package archives that point outside the package directory. Audit automation and CI/CD scripts for unexpected changes after package updates. Monitor for use of sensitive secrets (API keys, tokens) from unexpected locations or after package updates. Implement sandboxing (e.g., AppArmor) to restrict bot capabilities and prevent file system escape.
